name: Lucas Fernando
event: UFC Fight Night: Bonfim vs. Brady
summary: A tall Brazilian light heavyweight (14-3, age 30; about 6-foot-4) and former two-division LFA champion, on a five-fight win streak with four straight stoppages. He debuted in August with a third-round TKO of Rafael Tobias in which he out-landed him heavily with kicks at every level. Very active: November 7 will be his third fight in about five months.

how_they_fight.Striking: Range kickboxer with power. Against Tobias he used the jab to control distance and set up heavy calf kicks, body kicks and right hands, dropped Tobias with a jab-right sequence in R2, and threw wheel and head kicks (Cageside Press, LowKick). Rotowire counted a 69-13 significant-strike edge. Eight KO/TKO wins: six in R1, one in R3 (Tobias, knee to the body then elbows), one in R4 of a five-round LFA middleweight title fight.
how_they_fight.Grappling: Mostly defensive. Got back up quickly when Tobias caught a kick and took him down (LowKick). Two early regional submission wins (2018, 2019). On the Contender Series in 2023 he went 3 for 10 on takedowns and split control time evenly with Cesar Almeida, but lost the striking 28-71.
how_they_fight.Defense: Never stopped: all three losses were decisions (Diego Dias 2020, Cesar Almeida on DWCS 2023, Azamat Bekoev over five rounds in LFA in 2023). The Almeida loss, at middleweight, is the template for beating him: out-volume him and stay busy.
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: Early finisher who can also close late. Ten of 14 wins were stoppages: eight in R1, one in R3, one in R4; his last two LFA wins took 63 and 88 seconds. He went 25 minutes with Bekoev (a loss) and won another five-rounder by R4 TKO, so his gas tank is proven. Against Tobias he was more patient in R3, waited after buckling him with a leg kick, then finished with a body knee.
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Patient once ahead; picks strikes rather than rushing. Said he nearly quit after the Contender Series loss and credits his wife for keeping him in the sport (Boxing News, citing Sherdog and MMA Fighting). Spent a month in the US before his debut.

patterns: Jab and calf kicks to set up body kicks, right hands and knees
Seven R1 stoppages; last two LFA wins inside 90 seconds
Can finish late too: R3 TKO in UFC debut, R4 TKO in an LFA title fight
Never finished; all three losses on the cards
concerns: Only one UFC fight, against a winless opponent
Lost the volume battle badly to Almeida (2023)
Short turnaround: third fight since late May
Record differs by source: LowKick said the debut win made him 9-1; our data and most outlets have 14-3
keys_to_beat: Take away his range: pressure him, clinch, and wrestle
Check the calf kicks early so he can't build from them

news.text: Booked against Billy Elekana for Nov. 7 at UFC Vegas 124.
Debuted with a TKO (knee to the body and elbows) of Rafael Tobias at 1:10 of R3 at UFC 330.
Defended the LFA light heavyweight title with a 1:28 R1 TKO of Leon Soares before signing.
Said he considered quitting after his 2023 Contender Series loss.
